message.content:
LeBron James is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes in the history of the sport. Born on December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio, he rose to prominence as a high school phenom at St. Vincent‑St. Mary High School, where he was named the USA Today High School Player of the Year and led his team to a state championship.

He entered the NBA directly from high school in 2003, being selected first overall by the Cleveland Cavaliers. LeBron quickly became known for his exceptional combination of size, athleticism, court vision, and basketball IQ. He has won multiple NBA championships (2012, 2013, 2016, 2020) with the Miami Heat, Cleveland Cavaliers, and Los Angeles Lakers, earning NBA Finals MVP honors each time.

Beyond his on‑court achievements—four NBA Most Valuable Player awards, 19 All‑NBA selections, and numerous scoring and rebounding records—LeBron is also recognized for his philanthropy, notably the LeBron James Family Foundation, which opened the I PROMISE School, a public school for at‑risk children in his hometown. He has also pursued a career in entertainment, producing films and television shows, and remains a prominent voice on social and political issues.
